# DESIGN.md

<!-- Generated by `npm run system` from design/system.yaml: change the record, not this file. -->

**Starter.** A neutral starting point, not a style: a warm off-white page, one accent for every action, large and few headings, and a different shape for each section.

The tokens are compiled into `styles/theme.css`; the lint (`npm run lint`) reads the Declared section.

## Identity

```text
Subject:            to fill: what this site sells, explains, or does
Audience:           to fill: who arrives, and what they already know
One job:            to fill: what the page must make clear or help someone do
Direction:          to fill: the chosen direction's name and one-sentence thesis
Source:             to fill: the real-world artifact or behaviour it borrows from
Signature:          to fill: the one moment a visitor should remember
Rejection:          to fill: the familiar pattern this site deliberately avoids
Photography:        to fill: real photos the owner has, or the honest slot until they do
```

## Visual Theme & Atmosphere

A warm, quiet page that lets one thing be loud at a time. The ground is a warm off-white, not pure white; the text is a near-black with brown in it; one saturated accent does every action. Headings are large and few, set at nine to twelve characters per line, so hierarchy comes from size and space rather than from weight or decoration. Every section is composed differently from the one before it. Colour and energy belong to the content (photos, work, the brand's own material), not to the chrome around it. This is the starting point, not a brand: the site's own system replaces it.

## Color Palette & Roles

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| `canvas` | #f6f3ec |
| `surface` | #fffdf8 |
| `panel` | #ebe5d8 |
| `night` | #14110d |
| `ink` | #191612 |
| `ink-2` | #57514a |
| `ink-3` | #6b5f54 |
| `night-ink` | #f6f3ec |
| `night-ink-2` | #bfb6aa |
| `accent` | #2f5bea |
| `accent-ink` | #ffffff |
| `accent-hover` | color-mix(in oklab, `accent` 85%, black) |
| `line` | rgb(25 22 18 / 0.14) |
| `line-strong` | rgb(25 22 18 / 0.32) |
| `line-on-night` | rgb(246 243 236 / 0.16) |

`canvas` is the page ground; most sections sit on it. `surface` is a raised card or framed visual on the canvas. `panel` is one step down, a tinted band: at most two per page, never adjacent. `night` is the dark ground: the footer and at most one statement band, never a card. `ink` is headings and body on light grounds, `ink-2` secondary text, `ink-3` captions and metadata (never a border); on night, `night-ink` and `night-ink-2`. `accent` is the one action colour: primary buttons, links in body copy, the focus ring; `accent-ink` is text on it and `accent-hover` its hover. `line` is every hairline on light grounds, `line-strong` input edges and table frames, `line-on-night` hairlines on night. Text meets 4.5:1 on its ground; focus rings and input edges 3:1. Photographs and the brand's own artwork carry colour; the interface around them stays in this palette.

## Typography Rules

| Class | Family | Size | Line height | Tracking | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `text-display` | Bricolage Grotesque | clamp(3rem, 8vw, 6rem) | 0.95 | -0.03em | 700 |
| `text-section` | Bricolage Grotesque | clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 3.75rem) | 1 | -0.025em | 600 |
| `text-title` | Bricolage Grotesque | clamp(1.5rem, 2.4vw, 2rem) | 1.1 | -0.015em | 600 |
| `text-lede` | Inter | clamp(1.125rem, 1.4vw, 1.375rem) | 1.5 |  | 400 |
| `text-copy` | Inter | 1.125rem | 1.6 |  | 400 |
| `text-specimen` | Bricolage Grotesque | clamp(6rem, 18vw, 11rem) | 1 | -0.03em | 600 |
| `text-label` | Inter | 0.8125rem | 1.4 | 0.04em | 600 |

Two families: a display face for headings, a text face for reading. `text-display` is the h1 of the home page or a landing page, one per page, 9 to 12 characters per line. `text-section` is every h2; beside a visual it wraps at 10 to 16ch. `text-title` is the h3 of a row, a card or a callout. `text-lede` is the supporting thought under a heading, max-w-xl, in `ink-2`. `text-copy` is body copy, the default, under 70 characters a line. `text-label` is the one small label style, for metadata; nothing renders smaller. `text-specimen` is one giant glyph or word inside a visual (role="img"), never a heading. Headings use font-display; a heading never goes above 700 and body copy is always 400. No tracking-* or leading-* on text that has a size token; the token carries both.

## Component Stylings

Buttons (Button in src/components): 48px minimum, px-5, `rounded-control`, 16px semibold. Primary is `accent` under `accent-ink`, hover `accent-hover`; secondary is a `line-strong` outline with a `panel` hover. One primary per section; the label says what happens next ("Book a call", never "Learn more"). Links in copy are underlined, 1px, offset, in the text's colour. Nav links are `ink-2`, `ink` on hover, with aria-current="page" on the current page. Cards only for discrete, comparable objects (a service, a person, a plan, a review): `rounded-card`, `line` edge, `surface`; never around a single paragraph. Inputs are 48px tall, `rounded-control`, a `line-strong` edge, the label above in 16px semibold, help text in `ink-3`. Lists of rows: divide-y with generous py-8, a numeral or small object on the left, a title and a sentence on the right; prefer rows to three cards in a grid. Images at `rounded-card` or `rounded-frame`, real alt text, object-cover.

## Layout Principles

The base unit is 4px. Sections take py-section (clamp(5rem, 10vw, 8.5rem)); a heading group to what it introduces is mt-lead (clamp(2.5rem, 4vw, 3.5rem)). Every band shares one frame, max-w-wide (80rem) with px-5 sm:px-8 at the sides (Section does this), so the header, each section and the footer start on one left edge; a reading section narrows its column inside the frame to max-w-content (72rem), left aligned. A photograph or colour field runs edge to edge behind the frame. Compose from the content: a sequence, a comparison, a hierarchy and a change of thought each look different. No two adjacent sections share a composition or a ground. One section is the peak; everything else is quieter. Prefer document flow; absolute positioning is for one deliberate layer, never the skeleton.

## Depth & Elevation

Three levels. Flat: sections, rows, text, most of the page. Lifted: a card or framed visual on the canvas, a `line` edge plus `shadow-lift`, for the one visual that should feel like an object. Overlay: a menu or dialog on `surface` with `shadow-lift` at `rounded-card`. No inner shadows, no glass or blur, no gradients on interface elements.

## Motion

The first screen's words rise in once on load (data-rise on their wrapper), and one or two later bands as they come into view (data-reveal); a wall of reviews or logos may drift sideways (data-drift); nothing else moves. Hover and focus transitions are 150ms with `ease-soft`. Reduced motion shows the finished page (styles/input.css).

## Responsive Behavior

Mobile and desktop are two compositions of the same content. Type sizes are fluid, so headings need no mobile overrides. Below 1024px a split stacks with the text first unless the visual is the point; rows stay rows; cards go to one column below 640px. Touch targets are at least 44px, buttons 48px. The header is one row at every width; past four nav links the rest go into a menu. Check 390px and 1280px and one width between, with a long word and a long label. Semantic landmarks, one h1, visible focus and useful alt text are part of it.

## Do's and Don'ts

Do:

- Start from the brief and the real content; lock the words before the layout.
  A layout drawn before the words fits placeholder lengths, and real copy then breaks it or gets cut to fit.
- Spend boldness in one place per page.
  When every section is loud, none is; the peak is what a visitor remembers.
- Use the tokens; add a token to this record when one is missing.
  A one-off value in markup is a second design system that nobody maintains.
- Keep body copy at 18px with a measure under 70 characters.
  Small text and long lines are the first things that make a page tiring to read on a phone.

Don't:

- Don't default to a centred hero over a glow, a logo strip, three feature cards, testimonials, pricing, an FAQ and a final call to action.
  It is the generated-page template; a visitor has seen it a hundred times and it says nothing about this business.
- Don't use icons in coloured circles as the visual language.
  They fill space without showing anything real about the work.
- Don't show proof that is not real: invented customers, quotes, counts, awards or prices.
  One fake detail spoils every true one beside it.
- Don't use gradients, blur, glass or glow to make up for a weak idea.
  Effects date fast and hide that the section has nothing to show.

## Known Gaps

No photography rules and no layout rules per kind of content: those come with the site's own system.

## Changing the design

Edit `design/system.yaml` and run `npm run system`; then `npm run verify`.
A new brand colour or font goes into the record's tokens by role, never into markup. How a record is
written, and how it grows from the first homepage, is the `design` skill.
